verification.summary: PASS 67/67 checks: 24 schema round-trip checks (8 record types, lossless YAML and JSON), 15 schema refusal vectors each with a named reason (shell_plan/command fields, non-catalog operation, scenario outside domain, max_rounds 0/9, missing correlation identity, label outside frozen answer domain, hand-authored mechanism, unknown classification, retained-not-eligible, fingerprint mismatch, fabricated acceptance, route-depth over bound), 7 admission classification vectors (one per classification incl. both denied forms), 8 selection-policy unit vectors (baseline beats boundary, exactly one retained, midpoint wins, tie to smaller rounds, tie to lexicographic id, r*-1 priority over midpoint, ineligible-but-judgment-preferred not retained, zero payment retains nothing), provider-capability source scan of admission.py and selection_policy.py clean, catalog integrity (24 ops, full 3x8 coverage, provenance pinned and files exist on disk), prereg frozen sha256 matches disk, and evidence-manifest hash check verified all 5 frozen files (fail-closed path active).
verify-ruler.sh: PASS - answer key and manifest digests match the frozen lock (.gauntlet/reference.lock). Read-only digest tripwire; ruler untouched.

deviations: Ordering rules 1-3 implemented as tiered precedence: rule 1 (completes an unmet route-goal prerequisite) > rule 3 (r*-1 boundary priority) > rule 2 (midpoint heuristic) > other candidates. The prereg lists the rules 1-3 and gives rule 3 the wording 'has boundary priority'; we read it as outranking the rule-2 midpoint heuristic because otherwise the frozen boundary goal (both r* and r*-1 probed on this route) could not close. Recorded in the selection_policy docstring and b1-progress.md.

insufficient_evidence clause: 'whose consequence would be cited by the settlement criterion' is read as covering all three expected_roles (route_goal_frozen cites baseline, discriminator, and boundary consequences), so insufficient_evidence always disqualifies retention.

redundant is defined as (scenario, max_rounds) already probed on THIS route (neighborhood rule (a)); the prereg freezes no automatic cross-route duplicate rejection ('duplicates are measured and recorded; no automatic rejection is frozen in this slice'), so novelty-required is route-local.

Admission classification precedence is fixed and documented (non-mapping invalid; authority violations denied before schema-invalid; then prior-denial denied, unreachable, unaffordable, redundant, admitted). The prereg does not order overlapping violations; each gate vector exercises exactly one violation so the frozen expected outcomes are independent of this choice.

unreachable = the candidate's scenario does not resolve to a pinned fixture path in the operations catalog (the gate separately verifies those pinned files exist on disk). admission.py performs no filesystem access, keeping it free of os-path/provider capability.

probe_observation.terminal_class uses the task-contract vocabulary settled|budget_exhausted|other-nonsettlement|run_error while judgment labels use the frozen answer domain; the coarse-to-fine terminal-to-label mapping is T22's judgment adapter and is intentionally not implemented in T21.

selection_record.policy_version is pinned to 'selection-policy-v1' by schema; a selection record declaring any other policy version is refused (corrections would use an append-only addendum and round-2+ paths).

A candidate dict missing identity fields still yields a schema-valid admission_decision using the placeholder identity 'unknown-candidate'/'unidentifiable-input' with the defect named in the reason, because every emitted decision must itself be a typed record.
route_state enforces the frozen bounds (max 5 retained moves, max 12 probes, probes_remaining 0..12) as schema constraints; the prereg freezes these bounds but does not say where they are enforced.
notes: T21 contract freeze complete with zero execution: no route loop, no probe, no provider call, no gauntlet run, and no cargo/nextest/just besides the single read-only `just ruler` tripwire. Deliverables implement the frozen prereg (sha256 1fb55d9c56d87d94adc4850bc5ca713db3e600297fbdc997accfab54c98ea8b5, recomputed from disk and pinned in evidence-manifest.yml): route_contracts.py (8 inert typed records with strict field sets, named refusal reasons, lossless YAML/JSON round-trips, route_fingerprint helper for the novelty metric), operations_catalog.yaml (24 run_case operations, full 3x8 coverage, per-operation derivation provenance pointing at the existing mock_runner_scenarios fixtures and the GAUNTLET.md max_rounds lever, neighborhood_rule restated as data), admission.py (classify() returning schema-valid admission_decision records; denied/invalid decisions are plain data with no execution path - the T22 loop executes only 'admitted'), selection_policy.py (selection-policy-v1 exactly as preregistered; consumes only typed records validated through route_contracts; no provider interface - enforced by source scan), verify_contract.py (the gate; manifest hash check fails closed on any mismatch). No script was modified after the manifest freeze; the gate passed 67/67 on its first and only official run.
